Many hPSC‐CM differentiation protocols rely on the use of recombinant human albumin and varying cocktails of chemicals to generate sufficient hPSC‐CMs. However, we have eliminated the use of these compounds because they may disrupt hPSC‐CM integrity and contribute to variability in differentiation efficiency. When hPSCs were differentiated into cardiomyocytes using CDM3 (which contains albumin, RPMI medium, and AA2P) versus AA2P alone, no statistical significance in the expression of the canonical cardiac marker, TNNT2, was observed (Fig. 2A). Furthermore, there was no significance in TNNT2 expression between the use of AA2P versus B27 supplement (which contains complex fatty acids, proteins, enzymes, etc.), indicating that AA2P alone is sufficient to generate hPSC‐CMs (Fig. 2A). To identify the optimal concentration of AA2P required for differentiation, a range of AA2P concentrations were tested (Fig. 2B). Although expression of TNNT2 could be achieved at 64, 128, 256, and 512 µg/ml, higher AA2P concentrations were not observed to enhance the expression levels of TNNT2. To validate differentiated cardiomyocytes, expressing cardiac‐specific proteins, we performed immunofluorescence microscopy on day 20 hPSC‐CMs in culture. Immunofluorescence images showed that the hPSC‐CMs expressed both filamentous actin (F‐actin) and cardiac α‐actinin (a marker of the Z‐disc) (Fig. 2C). Therefore, successful directed hPSC‐CM differentiation can be achieved using minimal components that are protein‐ and xenobiotic‐free. Moreover, the cost associated with hPSC cardiac differentiation is significantly reduced (Table 1), which can facilitate large‐scale projects.

steps.title: Coat culture plates
steps.instruction: Thaw Matrigel GFR (cat. 356231) on ice or keep recombinant vitronectin (VTN‑N, cat. A14700) at 4 °C; dilute Matrigel 1:30 in cold DMEM/F12 (cat. 10‑092‑CM) or use vitronectin at 5 µg cm⁻², add 1 ml per well of a 6‑well plate, incubate 5–30 min, then let plates rest 16 h at 4 °C or 1 h at room temperature before use.

steps.title: Thaw and plate hPSCs
steps.instruction: Quick‑thaw a cryovial containing ~1–2 × 10⁶ hPSCs in a 37 °C water bath, transfer to a 15‑ml conical tube with 10 ml pre‑warmed E8 medium (cat. A1517001) containing 10 µM Y‑27632 (cat. 1254), centrifuge 200 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend the pellet in E8 + Y‑27632, and seed 1 ml per well onto the coated plates; incubate 24 h before the first medium change.

steps.title: Feed hPSCs daily
steps.instruction: Warm E8 medium to 37 °C (≈20 min), aspirate spent medium, add 2 ml fresh E8 per well, and repeat each day; daily feeding takes ~5–10 min per plate.

steps.title: Passage hPSCs
steps.instruction: When colonies reach 70–80 % confluence, wash wells with 1× PBS (cat. 10010002), add Cell Dissociation Buffer (CDB, cat. 13151014), incubate 5 min at 37 °C, gently detach cells, collect the suspension, centrifuge 200 × g for 5 min, resuspend in E8 + Y‑27632, and seed onto freshly coated plates at the desired density; passage takes ~15–20 min per 6‑well plate.

steps.title: Cryopreserve hPSCs
steps.instruction: Harvest cells as for passage, resuspend at 1–2 × 10⁶ cells ml⁻¹ in Bambanker medium (cat. 302‑14681), aliquot 1 ml into cryovials, place vials in a -80 °C freezer using a controlled‑rate container for 10–15 min, then transfer to liquid nitrogen for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Prepare AA2P base medium
steps.instruction: In a sterile bottle combine DMEM/F12 (50:50) with l‑glutamine and 15 mM HEPES (cat. 10‑092‑CM), add l‑ascorbic acid 2‑phosphate (AA2P) powder (cat. 49752‑100G) to a final concentration of 64, 128, 256 or 512 µg ml⁻¹ (test range), add 60 % (w/w) sodium d‑lactate solution (cat. L4263‑500ML) to the desired final lactate concentration, and supplement with RPMI‑1640 without glucose (cat. 11879020) as needed; filter‑sterilize and store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Add CHIR99021 and IWR‑1
steps.instruction: To the AA2P base medium add CHIR99021 (cat. 4423) to a final concentration of 3–6 µM (optimize per cell line) for the initial Wnt‑activation phase; after the CHIR exposure period replace medium with AA2P base medium containing IWR‑1‑endo (cat. S7086) at the appropriate inhibitory concentration for the Wnt‑inhibition phase.

steps.title: Start cardiomyocyte differentiation
steps.instruction: On day 0 replace E8 medium with AA2P differentiation medium containing CHIR99021, incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂; after the CHIR treatment period (duration per protocol) change to AA2P medium with IWR‑1; continue daily medium changes for ~10 days, monitoring medium color (red = physiological pH, orange/yellow = increasing acidity). If the medium becomes bright yellow, either add extra AA2P medium during the second day of CHIR or IWR‑1 treatment, or increase the total volume of base medium added at each step.

steps.title: Purify cardiomyocytes with lactate
steps.instruction: Switch cultures to glucose‑free medium supplemented with sodium d‑lactate for 3 days (extend beyond 3 days if necessary) to selectively eliminate non‑cardiomyocyte cells; monitor cell death in the background and aim for >80 % cardiomyocyte purity.

steps.title: Immunofluorescence of hPSC‑CMs
steps.instruction: On day 20 wash cultures with DPBS without Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ (cat. 14190‑144), fix with 4 % formaldehyde (cat. 427098) for 10 min at room temperature, wash with DPBS, permeabilize with 0.1 % Triton X‑100 (cat. 85111) for 5 min, wash, block with 2 % BSA and 22.5 mg ml⁻¹ glycine in PBST (0.1 % Tween 20 in PBS) for 30 min, incubate overnight at 4 °C with mouse monoclonal anti‑α‑actinin (1:200, EA‑53), wash, incubate 1 h at room temperature with Alexa Fluor 405‑conjugated goat anti‑mouse IgG (per manufacturer) and simultaneously with Texas Red‑X Phalloidin (1:100, cat. T7471) for F‑actin, wash, mount coverslips with VECTASHIELD Antifade Mounting Media (cat. H‑1000‑10), and image.

steps.title: Capture and analyze images
steps.instruction: Acquire fluorescence images of α‑actinin (405 nm) and F‑actin (Texas Red) using a Nikon ECLIPSE Ts2 fluorescence microscope, process the images, and quantify cardiomyocyte markers; allocate ~2 days (2–3 h per day) for imaging and analysis.
